title: When the Mixtape Breaks
premise: Coral Ishikawa has spent three years being invisible: eldest of four, surrogate parent, honor roll ghost. When the school's legendary spirit — a student who died in 1987 — begins leaving her notes in ink that shifts color and can't be erased, she learns the ghost was also a caretaker sibling who traded her own name to the school's 'archive' in exchange for her brother's future. The archive is a living ledger beneath the school that consumes identities to grant wishes, and it's now hungry for Coral's younger siblings. To break the cycle, Coral must uncover the ghost's true name, offer her own in its place, and discover that a name freely given — rather than taken — can free everyone the archive has ever held. She ends the book choosing to be seen: keeping her name, freeing the ghost, and letting her family finally know who she really is.
about_author: Lena Eriksen is the pen name of a former night-shift nurse who wrote her first novel on break-room napkins. She lives in a coastal town full of old schools and older secrets, and writes stories about kids who carry too much.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A morning in the Ishikawa household: burnt toast, missing bus money, Coral forging a permission slip for her brother Ren. At school she's praised for being 'so mature' and feels it like a weight. Establishes her invisibility strategy and the family she's holding together. Emotional beat: competent exhaustion, love expressed as logistics.

chapters.title: The Ink That Wouldn't Dry
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She finds a note in her locker addressed to 'Coral' — no one at school uses her first name — written in ink that shimmers violet and won't smudge. The note says only: 'You count the exits too.' She checks the paper against every pen she owns. Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of being truly seen.

chapters.title: What Everyone Knows About the Ghost
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Her friend Dev gives her the school legend: in 1987 a senior named 'the Caretaker' died in the auditorium and still walks the halls. Coral notices the yearbook page for 1987 has been razored out. First supernatural escalation: her own handwriting briefly changes on a homework sheet. Emotional beat: curiosity overriding caution.

chapters.title: Second Note: The Price List
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The ghost leaves a page listing things students have traded: a stutter, a first kiss, a name. The last line: 'Your mother traded something the year you were born. Ask her.' Coral can't — mom works nights and sleeps through mornings. Emotional beat: dread that her family's struggles have a hidden cost.

chapters.title: Ren's Perfect Day
chapters.summary: Ren's POV. Coral's brother Ren, twelve, has an inexplicably perfect day — he aces a test he didn't study for, the girl he likes talks to him. He finds a note in his own locker: 'One wish, one trade.' He doesn't tell Coral. Emotional beat: the seductive ease of something too good to be true.

chapters.title: The Auditorium at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Unable to sleep, Coral sneaks into the school and meets the ghost: a girl in an outdated uniform who speaks in fragments. The ghost warns her about 'the Archive under the stage' and vanishes when the janitor's keys sound. Coral finds a 1987 playbill with the cast list — one name scratched out. Emotional beat: awe curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Mom, Awake for Once
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral catches her mother before a night shift and asks about 1987. Mom goes white and admits she attended the school; her sister — Coral's aunt — was the girl who died, and Mom has never spoken her name aloud since. She refuses to say it now. Emotional beat: the family secret cracks open, but not all the way.

chapters.title: Labels Off
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At school, the archive begins stripping labels: name tags blank, yearbooks blanked, teachers calling students 'hey, you.' Only Coral and Dev can still say names aloud. Ren's trade is revealed — he wished for Coral to 'have less to carry,' and the archive is taking her identity as payment. Emotional beat: guilt and fury at a wish made of love.

chapters.title: Dev Sees It Too
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev, who has always felt mislabeled by everyone's assumptions, admits he's been getting notes as well — the archive offered him a new name, one that fits. He hasn't answered yet. He and Coral compare notes and realize the ghost is protecting them from the archive, not haunting them. Emotional beat: alliance, and the temptation of a clean slate.

chapters.title: The Ledger Beneath the Stage
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral descends under the auditorium stage and finds the Archive: a room of shelves where every traded name is a physical book, pages still warm. Her aunt's book is there, spine blank, whispering. The archive speaks through the shelves, offering to restore everything — if Coral signs herself over. Emotional beat: vertigo before overwhelming power.

chapters.title: What the Archive Wants
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The archive explains its hunger: it keeps the school 'stable' by collecting identities, and it's running out — it needs a whole family's worth. It shows Coral visions of her siblings' bright futures, purchasable with her name. She refuses and runs, but the ink has marked her hand. Emotional beat: temptation reframed as corruption.

chapters.title: Ink Spreads
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The mark spreads; Coral's reflection blurs, teachers' eyes slide off her. Ren notices his sister 'going faint' and realizes what his wish cost. He tries to retract it; the archive refuses refunds. Emotional beat: sibling guilt meeting sibling forgiveness — Ren confesses, Coral doesn't blame him.

chapters.title: The Caretaker's Name
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The ghost appears fully for the first time and leads Coral to the razored yearbook page hidden in the drama prop loft. Her aunt's name: Mika Ishikawa. The ghost traded her name in 1987 to save Coral's mother's scholarship, and the archive kept her ever since. Emotional beat: grief and kinship across decades.

chapters.title: Rules of the Trade
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The ghost explains the archive's one loophole: a name given freely, with love and full knowledge, cannot be consumed — it breaks the ledger. But no one in forty years has managed it, because the archive always hides the truth from whoever trades. Coral begins planning. Emotional beat: hope with a razor edge.

chapters.title: Dev's Answer
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev, exhausted by being the wrong kind of visible, accepts the archive's offer of a fitting name. Coral arrives too late to stop the trade and watches his real name slide onto a shelf. Emotional beat: betrayal, then understanding — the archive doesn't trick, it offers exactly what you think you want.

chapters.title: The Family Meeting
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral tells her mother and siblings everything. Mom finally says 'Mika' aloud, and the ghost flickers stronger at the sound. The family agrees to the plan: at the school's anniversary assembly, they will give Coral's name back to her — aloud, with love — breaking the trade's terms. Emotional beat: the burden finally shared.

chapters.title: Assembly Day
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The archive, sensing the plan, locks down the school: doors seal, clocks stutter, the shelves below begin pulling names from every student. Coral must reach the stage while the archive floods her mind with visions of the easy life she could buy. Emotional beat: rising panic, held together by purpose.

chapters.title: What the Archive Offers Coral
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, interior. Trapped in a vision, Coral lives the life where she traded her name: siblings safe, mother rested, no weight. It's perfect, and it's not her. The ghost's voice — 'You count the exits too' — anchors her. She chooses the heavy, real life. Emotional beat: the climax of identity — choosing the burden that is hers.

chapters.title: The Name Given Freely
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. On stage, before the whole sealed school, Coral's family speaks her name with love, and Coral speaks it herself — claiming it rather than surrendering it. The ledger cracks; shelves spill names back to their owners, including Dev's and Mika's. The archive, unbound, dissolves into ordinary dust. Emotional beat: cathartic climax, power returned.

chapters.title: Mika, Unfinished
chapters.summary: Mika's POV. Freed after forty years, Mika gets one hour of daylight with her sister, now grown. They talk about everything lost and everything that survived. Mika chooses to move on rather than linger, leaving Coral her old prop-loft key. Emotional beat: tender farewell, grief with gratitude in it.

chapters.title: Labels On, Chosen
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. School returns to normal, but Coral doesn't: she runs for student council, signs her art with her full name, and lets a teacher see her tired. Ren carries some of the load now; Dev, name restored, relearns to like the one he has. Emotional beat: quiet transformation — being seen by choice.

chapters.title: Coda: The Mixtape Breaks
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Months later, Coral finds a final note in locker 114: Mika's old mixtape, labeled in shifting ink, with one line — 'For the next eldest. It gets lighter when you share it.' Coral tapes it to the auditorium door for whoever needs it next. Emotional beat: the cycle broken, the legacy kept — love passed forward, freely.
